headline: GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI's new model operates software, discovers zero-days
summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra scores 100% on ExploitBench and can autonomously discover unknown vulnerabilities, marking a significant shift in AI capabilities. It's rolling out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.
details: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-6 Astra, a new model designed to act as a full computer operator rather than just a smarter API. It achieves extraordinary benchmark numbers, including 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4, and a perfect 100% on ExploitBench, supporting over one million tokens of context.

Astra's core innovation is its ability to operate software directly. It can browse the web, use a desktop, inspect codebases, execute shell commands, edit files, and manage multi-step tasks across various tools and applications autonomously.

This capability extends to cybersecurity, where Astra is the first broadly deployed model to reach the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework. Expert evaluations show it autonomously discovered unknown vulnerabilities and built working exploit chains against hardened targets.

Despite its advanced capabilities, Astra presents a complex safety profile. While it's reported to be better at respecting restrictions than its predecessor, GPT-5.6 Sol, it is also harder to monitor through its chain of thought, posing a central deployment challenge for enterprises.

GPT-6 Astra is now rolling out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers, as well as via the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Bedrock. Enterprise access is initially disabled by default and requires administrator activation.

Pro, Business, and Enterprise users will also gain access to the enhanced GPT-6 Astra Pro. OpenAI confirms that Astra usage will generally fall within existing subscription allowances, with additional credits available for extensive use.

The Responses API for Astra supports a wide range of functions, including web search, file search, image generation, Code Interpreter, hosted shell, and tool search. However, it does not currently support Realtime, Live, fine-tuning, embeddings, or native audio output.

While the million-token context window is powerful for large tasks like legal research or code investigations, OpenAI cautions against simply dumping all data. Usage above 272,000 input tokens incurs higher charges, and large contexts can introduce latency and quality issues, emphasizing the continued need for context engineering.

headline_marked: [[Google no longer provides direct URLs]] in search results, impacting scrapers
headline: Google no longer provides direct URLs in search results, impacting scrapers
summary: Google Search has started rewriting organic result links to an opaque google.com/goto?url=... format, a move that significantly raises the cost of automated SERP scraping. This change is consistent for logged-out and private browsing sessions.
details: Google Search has implemented a significant change, replacing direct destination URLs in organic search results with google.com/goto?url=... redirects. This new format uses a custom, Google-specific encoding for the target URL, making it opaque. The change has been consistently observed since late August 2026 for logged-out and private browsing sessions.

Previously, Google used google.com/url?q=[URL-encoded destination] for redirects, where the target URL was still readable in the query string. The new goto format, however, requires an additional request back to Google to resolve the actual destination.

This shift is a strategic move by Google to combat automated SERP harvesting, particularly from AI crawlers and SEO scrapers. With plaintext links, scrapers could extract thousands of URLs without further interaction with Google, but the goto links force each result to generate a request to Google's servers.

The requirement to resolve each goto link makes scraping slower, noisier, and provides Google with clear signals when a client attempts to resolve numerous links in sequence. This increases the operational cost for entities attempting to build their own search indexes from SERP data.

This change aligns with Google's broader efforts to deter naive SERP scraping, following previous measures like removing &num=100 and strengthening BotGuard/SearchGuard. The goal is to steadily raise the barriers for automated data extraction.

Companies like Autom, which provide Google Search endpoints, have already updated their pipelines to resolve these google.com/goto links. They ensure customers continue to receive usable destination URLs without needing to change their integrations, by reading the Location header without following through to the page.
